content.thinking:
I'm planning a hunched lava golem design in Genshin cel-shaded style, roughly 2.6m tall, with basalt body paints and glowing magma seam details, pulling in the builder, THREE, rng, and paint utilities I'll need to construct it.

Mapping out which builder API calls to use (part, rod, capsule, spike, extrude, lathe) and sketching a helper for faceted boulder shapes via icosahedron geometry, making sure feet rest at y=0. Defining a basalt/gold/lava color palette using cel paints with mottle textures for surface variation.

Now working out the body layout: legs and feet positioned symmetrically, calves and thighs as scaled icosahedron boulders, with glowing lava-seam torus rings at the ankles to simulate molten joints, moving next into the pelvis section.

Continuing upward I'm placing the hunched torso and chest with front armor plates, a glowing core sphere wrapped in a gold ring facing forward, basalt spikes on the back, then massive shoulder boulders trimmed in gold with their own spikes before heading into the arm geometry.

Now I'm sketching out the arms as tapering basalt rods from shoulder to elbow to fist, with glowing lava cracks running along them, and a small sunken head nestled between the shoulders with two glowing yellow eye spheres peeking out front.

Adding dark brow slabs, a jagged glowing mouth made of small boxes, and gold-tipped dark spikes rising as horns from the head, bringing total height to roughly 3.3 meters including the horn tips. I'm now working out jagged lava crack seams as sweep polylines running across the torso, thighs, and back, making sure each crack sits properly on the ellipsoid torso surface.

Tweaking seam factor to 1.01 with radius .028 so the crack looks slightly buried. For armor plates, I'm planning a helper that orients boxes outward along the ellipsoid's surface normal at given points, using lookAt-style orientation to place them like slab plates. For gold filigree, I'm thinking rings around wrists and shoulders plus a tasseled belt trim.

Now I'm working out the pelvis gold belt as a flattened torus—rotating it 90° to lie flat and scaling its local axes to squash it into an ellipse, positioned around y1.5 to wrap the pelvis shape, with hanging tassels made from small rods and sphere ends looped around it.

For the chest medallion, I'm designing a gold sun motif: a glowing core ring with eight spike rays radiating outward in the XY plane, each spike computed from an angle and direction vector so they fan out evenly from the center. I'm skipping extra floor details like ember rocks to keep things simple.

For the back, I'm adding a cluster of hexagonal basalt columns (using low-poly cylinder geometry) emerging from the upper back and leaning backward, each with a glowing cap built from a small cone at the tip -- a signature crystalline/volcanic look. I'm also planning mottled lava texture detailing across the surface.

Now I'm setting up paint functions for the lower legs and basalt areas, layering a cel-shaded base color with a darker ember-rock tint below a certain height threshold. I'm skipping the lava eye decals but adding angled dark eyebrow slabs, and giving the fists basalt knuckle spikes for extra texture.

I'm positioning four small knuckle spikes per fist pointing forward-up, spaced across the fist's width, then adding a golden trim ring (torus) around the top of each shoulder pauldron to sit flush with the boulder's curve.

Now I'm adding basalt spikes jutting outward-up from the shoulders, three per side, and setting up the code structure with typed arrays for points, color strings for glow effects, and a helper function to compute positions on an ellipsoid surface using azimuth and elevation angles.

Still writing geometry code...

Still defining body parts... gold ankle torus rings, glowing eye spheres, a jiggling row of mouth boxes, and a dark lower jaw boulder.
